## Description {#details}

<p>Deprecated overloaded operators for test comparisons.</p>


<p>The overloaded operators <span class="doxyComputerOutput">==</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">!=</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">&lt;</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">&gt;</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">&lt;=</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">&gt;=</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">and</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">or</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">not</span> are defined in the dedicated <span class="doxyComputerOutput">micro_test_plus::operators</span> namespace, to avoid conflicts with application-defined operators.</p>


<dl class="doxySectionUser">
<dt>Deprecated</dt>
<dd><p>The operators are deprecated since 5.1.0, in favour of the function comparators <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::eq()</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::ne()</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::lt()</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::le()</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::gt()</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::ge()</span>, and of the logical functions <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::all_of()</span>, <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::any_of()</span>, and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::negate()</span>, which check and report the plain values, without literal suffixes or casts. The compiler reports the use of the operators.</p></dd>
</dl>


<p>The operators are restricted to the framework types (see <span class="doxyComputerOutput">extension::is_op</span>). For constant values, this is achieved with the (deprecated) literals, for example <span class="doxyComputerOutput">1_i</span>, whilst dynamic values can be wrapped with the (deprecated) converters such as <span class="doxyComputerOutput">mt::to_i{expression}</span>. When neither operand is of such a type, the standard operators are selected; they return a plain <span class="doxyComputerOutput">bool</span>, so a failed check cannot show the operands.</p>



:::warning
<p>The overloaded <span class="doxyComputerOutput">and</span> and <span class="doxyComputerOutput">or</span> operators evaluate both operands before the check, so they do not short-circuit like the built-in ones.</p>
:::
